I have 200 mu to manage this year. That is a lot of land for just me, my wife, and the two kids helping when they can. I finished middle school and I have been farming only four years, so I still follow what the older farmers around me do, but I also read the bags and listen to the dealer in town.

My main land is wheat-maize, same as most people in Quzhou. I will put 150 mu into the wheat-maize rotation — wheat through the winter, then maize right after the wheat comes off in June. For cabbage I will use 30 mu — it sells well at the vegetable market and cabbage likes our well water. Stevia I will keep at 20 mu; the company buys it on contract and the price is steady.

For wheat, I will use the improved variety "Jimai 22" like my neighbor Old Wang — he got over 500 kg/mu last year. I will put down about 18 kg N per mu, half as base fertilizer (compound 15-15-15, about 40 kg/mu) and the other half as urea at the green-up stage. Phosphorus around 9 kg/mu, potassium around 7 kg/mu, all in the base. I will irrigate four times — before sowing, at green-up, jointing, and grain-filling. Spray pesticide twice, once for aphids and once for wheat rust.

For maize, hybrid seed — Zhengdan 958 works in our area. I apply 17 kg N/mu, 6 kg P, 6 kg K. One top-dressing at the big-flare stage. I only irrigate twice because summer rain helps. Two sprays for corn borer.

Cabbage needs a lot of feeding. I will use 22 kg N, 10 kg P, 12 kg K per mu, irrigate 6 times from the well, and spray 4 times for caterpillars and aphids. Hybrid seed from the county shop.

Stevia I treat lightly — 10 kg N, 5 kg P, 6 kg K, irrigate 3 times, spray twice.

I plough the wheat ground once a year in autumn to bury the maize stubble, but for summer maize after wheat I only rotary-till — no time to deep plough between crops. Cabbage and stevia beds I plough each planting.

I would rather put a bit of extra fertilizer than come up short. Losing yield on 150 mu of wheat would hurt much more than spending a few hundred extra yuan on urea.
